comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh full-restart verification on27October2026. Adopted TiSEM EER2026–2027v4 pp65–67 fixes the English BSc E&BI2026-entry pathway across2026–2029:180EC,60peryear. All named first/second-year courses compulsory;year3 includes30ECapproved mobility/minor/internship space,6ECPhilosophyforBusiness,12ECGraduationProject,one6ECspecialisation andone6ECprogramme elective. Restricted choices are instantiated independently of UCR fit by formal EER list order:AdvancedStartupEntrepreneurship andInternationalEntrepreneurship. These are course choices,not an invented formal route. GROW0EC is explicitly noncompulsory and highly recommended in every semester. EER3.7 governs elective approval/nonoverlap;4.4–4.7 and5.6 govern progression,project/internship eligibility,manual requirements and assessed-practical attendance conditions. Formal E&BI learning outcomes onp65 also substantiate entrepreneurial research synthesis and presentation;the affected programme-interest row links that adopted source explicitly.

core: Entrepreneurship, venture creation, entrepreneurial mindset and business innovation
Business foundations, accounting, finance, economics and law
Market opportunities, entrepreneurial marketing, business models and problem-solution fit
Quantitative methods, programming and data-driven decisions
Leadership, ethics, teams, creative problem-solving and deal-making
Evidence-based entrepreneurial practice, research, pitching and graduation work
adjacent: Corporate entrepreneurship, digital innovation and change inside organisations
Impact entrepreneurship and sustainable, socially valuable ventures
questions: How can an entrepreneur identify an opportunity, test problem-solution fit and build a viable business model?
How can entrepreneurial thinking and digital tools drive innovation inside an existing organisation?
How can ventures create economic value while producing social or environmental impact?

alternatives.label: Entrepreneurial ventures & business innovation
alternatives.concept: Venture creation and business innovation connect customer needs, product development, marketing, finance, economics and organisational leadership. Quantitative and qualitative research, communication and negotiation support evidence-based entrepreneurial decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has direct venture creation, product-development and business-strategy work, supported by market research, marketing, finance, leadership and evidence. The label describes that substance without claiming the four-project Tilburg sequence.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, leadership and communication foundations precede advanced strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, econometrics, market research and international governance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Corporate innovation & business analytics
alternatives.concept: Venture and product development, business strategy and organisational study examine innovation inside established firms. Programming, data science, quantitative analysis and AI ethics provide tools for assessing digital opportunities and responsible strategic change.
alternatives.labelReason: The reconstructed programme retains venture/product development, marketing, market research, business law, negotiation, leadership, accounting and strategy. Its programming, mathematics, database and AI-ethics strand implements the explicit data/AI learning line without allowing algorithms and deep learning to displace too much business substance.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses differ from the broad option(45EC):programming,mathematicalmethods,linearalgebra,probability/statistics,database systems andAIethics. These tools alter the mode of business analysis while direct venture/product/strategy/market work remains central; the option does not reproduce a formal Tilburg corporate specialisation.
progression: Programming and mathematical foundations precede their applications;MathematicalMethods precedes LinearAlgebra andProbabilityStatistics;business/research gateways precede all dependent law,negotiation,marketing and marketresearch courses. ConsumerProductDesign and applied business inquiry provide substantive venture/innovation work. All72placements across the final three alternatives were checked against actual prerequisites and six assigned offerings.

alternatives.label: Impact entrepreneurship & sustainable ventures
alternatives.concept: Impact-oriented ventures combine customer-focused product design, business strategy, finance, marketing and leadership with climate, life-cycle assessment and circular-economy study. Environmental science, governance and sector cases define problems and interventions; business and research courses support decisions about viable and responsible ventures.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains substantial business and venture work while life-cycle assessment, climate, sustainability foundations, governance and energy/farming cases supply the impact domain. Environmental courses are complementary problem knowledge,not stand-ins for dedicated impact-entrepreneurship courses.
alternatives.distinctness: Nine courses differ from the broad option(67.5EC). Sustainability foundations,climate,life-cycle/circular-economy assessment,governance,farming/energy cases,ethics andpubliceconomics create a sustained impact focus. The prior resource-recovery chemistry lab is replaced by data inquiry,and financial decision-making replaces a second leadership course to strengthen entrepreneurial decisions.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

selection.assessment: Broad venture/businessinnovation first tested against defining target substance. Corporateinnovation/dataAI is the strongest additional official direction;its implementation is reconstructed to restore businesslaw,productdesign,econometrics and leadershipcommunication while dropping excess algorithms/deeplearning/generalpsychology. Sixcourse45ECdifference remains meaningful. Impactventures then passes with life-cycle/circular-economy and environmental intervention substance plus substantial businesscore;data andfinance replace weaker courseweight. All three concepts are independently evidenced and pairwise distinct;the maximum is reached after these sequential tests,not used as a target.

audience.programmeDescription: Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation at Tilburg University studies how new ventures and existing organisations develop ideas into economic and societal value. Business theory, quantitative methods, programming and personal development support four Entrepreneurship in Action projects and a graduation project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The broad UCR option combines venture and product development with marketing, finance, economics, leadership and research. The corporate option adds programming and quantitative business analytics; the impact option adds life-cycle assessment, sustainability and environmental intervention study. These programmes provide substantial related study while leaving gaps in Tilburg’s four-project practice sequence, dedicated entrepreneurship contexts and compulsory graduation project.

curriculum.routeLabel: 2026 entrants; English; Advanced Startup Entrepreneurship + International Entrepreneurship
curriculum.limitation: The 180-EC pathway follows the adopted rules for 2026 entrants. One 6-EC specialisation and one 6-EC elective are selected from restricted lists. The 30-EC mobility/minor/internship window remains approved choice space. GROW is optional and carries 0 EC.
